summary: This is a closed GitHub issue (#1478) in the ros2/ros2 repository, opened by RnoldR on Aug 28, 2023, reporting that installing ROS 2 Humble dependencies via rosdep as sudo causes a Python module import failure. The reporter's robot uses Adafruit and Sparkfun sensors; installing Adafruit-Blinka with sudo pip led to 'No module named hid' when running a VL53L1X distance sensor publisher node. Maintainer gavanderhoorn explained that rosdep runs installers as root by default and suggested '--as-root pip:no', which the reporter confirmed resolved the issue, and the issue was closed as completed.
one_line: GitHub issue #1478 in ros2/ros2: rosdep installing Adafruit-Blinka via sudo pip causes a missing 'hid' module error, fixed with --as-root pip:no.
key_facts: GitHub issue #1478 in the ros2/ros2 repository was titled 'Rosdep - installing as sudo results in dependency errors'.
RnoldR opened the issue on Aug 28, 2023 and it was closed as completed the same day.
The reporter was using Ubuntu 22.04 with ROS2 Humble and rosdep version 0.22.2.
The reporter's robot needed Adafruit and Sparkfun sensors and the reporter was experimenting with installing new drivers via a forked and modified rosdistro python.yaml.
Running the sensor_vl53l1x talker node failed with 'ModuleNotFoundError: No module named hid' when Adafruit-Blinka had been installed with sudo pip.
The reporter stated that installing as a normal user worked fine, while installing as sudo caused the error.
The reporter's package.xml listed python3-adafruit-blinka-pip and python3-adafruit-circuitpython-bno055-pip as exec_depend entries.
The traceback showed board.py importing adafruit_blinka and adafruit_platformdetect, which then failed on 'import hid'.
gavanderhoorn stated that rosdep installs as the super user by default because most of the installers it coordinates, such as apt, require it.
gavanderhoorn suggested passing the command line argument '--as-root pip:no' to make rosdep not use sudo for pip installers.
The reporter replied 'I was looking for that, thank you very much!' after the suggestion.
The reporter noted that pip warns against installing as root during installation.
